section.sectionSummaryBrief: Yaakov's descent into mundane matters after Tishrei is itself an ascent that brings joy and completeness, drawing G‑d's blessing in all areas.
section.t: And this may be connected to the matter of “and Yaakov went on his way”
(which occurs at the conclusion of Shabbat Parshas Noach49),
for although after the month of Tishrei he goes on his way
(also)
in matters of the permitted and in weekday activities,
even to the level of “many waters” mentioned above,
nevertheless, through this very thing he is elevated more,
becoming in the aspect of “movement”50,
as the verse states51
“and Yaakov went on his way.”
And this knowledge
[that the descent
(to his way in matters of the permitted, etc.)
is a need for ascent]
causes the going to be with joy and a good heart
[as it says52
regarding Yaakov, “and Yaakov lifted his feet etc.” when he was informed of good tidings etc.].
And this causes his service to be in the ultimate perfection and beyond measure and limitation
(the aspect of “with all your might”53),
for joy breaks through54
all boundaries.
And by his performing his service
[in all three lines
(the three sons of Noach55)
of Torah, service, and acts of kindness]
in ultimate perfection and with joy and a good heart,
there is drawn to him also the blessing of G‑d in all that he needs
[in the three matters of children, life, and sustenance56]
in ultimate perfection and with joy and a good heart,
both in spirituality and in physicality,
and in spirituality and physicality together.
